A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MLHCA and contain readable methods, equations, experiments, figures, tables, and appendices. Material moved into v2's reorganized appendices can be matched reliably to v1.

before.justification: Sections 4 and 6 and Appendices G and J report original valuation-learning experiments, auction simulations, bridge-bid ablations, and revenue results.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and reports additional comparator results and computational timings in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The mMVNN architecture, mixed DQ/VQ training, price generation, bridge bid, and marginal-economy queries are retained. V2 explains caching already reflected in v1's hyperparameter tables. Its positive-part notation leaves the exact-argmax training loss unchanged; the misreport-detection argument introduces no new auction step.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate valuation learning and spectrum allocation using GSVM, LSVM, SRVM, and MRVM. V2 documents these domains more fully, but introduces no new dataset, population, or task. Additional bidding heuristics remain comparisons within the existing auction tasks.

E2.justification: V2's Table 9 substantially expands the evaluated comparator set, adding ML-CCA with profit-max bids, CCA with raised bids or profit-max bids, MVNN, NN, Fourier-transform methods, and random search. V1 discusses or cites some of these approaches but does not report these corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 corrects the efficiency-loss formula from one minus optimal/achieved welfare to one minus achieved/optimal welfare. Table 9 adds supplementary-bidding protocols with larger query budgets and explicitly counts each profit-max bid as one query. The original 100-query comparisons and HPO settings remain unchanged; rerunning them is not established.

E4.justification: The mixed-query learning comparisons, bridge-bid ablation, and analyses of inferred versus true welfare are retained. V1's Section 6.2 analyses move to v2's Appendix G.8. The additional comparator scores do not constitute new ablation, robustness, or sensitivity tests.

E5.justification: Appendix G.1 newly specifies 100 auction instances and seeds 101–200, while the retained efficiency figures still specify 50 instances. Bridge-bid captions also newly state 50 instances. This changes run-count documentation but does not reliably establish increased runs. The existing 95% confidence intervals and 5% t-test convention remain.

E6.justification: Table 9 adds substantial comparison results, including MRVM efficiency losses of 6.32% for ML-CCA with profit-max bids, 8.16% for MVNN, and 48.79% for random search. V2 also adds the GSVM efficiency trajectory and runtime measurements. Existing learning, principal efficiency, revenue, and bridge-bid results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds Lemma B.6 and its proof concerning positive fitting loss for inconsistent reports. It also revises the initial-query advantage proof to use growing item counts, i.i.d. prices, and Chebyshev's inequality. The principal impossibility, bridge-bid, and inductive-bias results are retained rather than newly introduced.

C1.justification: The hybrid-auction contribution and tenfold efficiency-loss claim remain. V2 changes the abstract's query-saving claim from 30% in MRVM to up to 58% across domains, adds an inconsistent-report detection claim, and corrects the joint BOCA/ML-CCA query threshold from 58 to 74 in the results discussion, consistent with unchanged Table 2.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly states that the VQ phase is not strategyproof and adds discussion of how the empirical results support the assumptions behind conditional truthfulness guarantees. Appendix G.4 newly interprets computational costs relative to auction timing. Existing explanations involving competition, bridge bids, and revenue remain.

D1.justification: Beyond v1's algorithms and HPO tables, v2 provides domain capacities and bidder counts, SATS version 0.8.1, seed identifiers, operating system and Python versions, CPU/RAM specifications, and per-domain runtimes. It also explains cached demand solutions and supplementary-bid generation. These substantially expand implementation and reproducibility documentation.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds discussion of LLM preference elicitation and mechanism design, citing Huang et al. (2025), Dütting et al. (2024), and Soumalias et al.'s LLM aggregation work. Domain descriptions add Goeree–Holt and Scheffel et al. citations. The central positioning relative to MLCA, ML-CCA, and BOCA remains.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title, extensively rewrites and condenses the introduction, theoretical exposition, learning discussion, and conclusion, and reorganizes the appendices into thematic groups. Detailed material formerly in the main text is retained in appendices, while the main experimental narrative gives priority to efficiency comparisons.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column main text and extensively relocates and resizes figures, tables, and algorithms. It adds the GSVM panel and expanded Table 9, duplicates the main learning table in the appendix, and separately redisplays the bridge-bid plot while preserving the original paired analysis.

improvement.justification: V2 improves assessability through broader comparator evidence, substantial runtime and implementation documentation, and corrections to the efficiency-loss formula and query-threshold discussion. The central method and principal measurements are unchanged. The gains are limited by remaining reporting problems, particularly the conflicting 100-versus-50 instance counts and inconsistent query-type labels in Table 9.
